chunks: ʿAlī ibn Mahzīyār, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from one who informed him, from one of the two (Imams) عليهما السلام, who said:

ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was brought a man who had killed another man’s brother. So he handed him over to him and ordered him to kill him. The man struck him until he thought that he had killed him, and he was carried to his home. They found in him some remaining life, so they treated him until he recovered. Then when he came out, the brother of the slain man seized him and said: “You are the killer of my brother, and I have the right to kill you.” He said to him: “You have already killed me once.” So he took him to ʿUmar, and he ordered that he be killed. Then he came out saying: “O people, by Allah, he has killed me.” They passed by with him to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, and he informed him of his case. So he said: “Do not hasten against him until I come out to you.” Then he entered upon ʿUmar and said: “The judgment regarding him is not like this.” He said: “What is it, O Abā al-Ḥasan?” He said: “This man should exact retaliation from the brother of the first slain man equal to what he did to him, then he may kill him for his brother.” So he realized that if he were to exact retaliation from him, it would destroy his own life; thus he pardoned him, and they left one another.

key_terms.الْحُكْمُ: the legal judgment or ruling in the case
key_terms.الْقَتْلِ: killing; taking a life in the legal context of homicide
key_terms.رَمَقًا: a remnant of life; a slight sign that life still remained
key_terms.عَفَا: he pardoned; he relinquished his right of retaliation
key_terms.يَقْتَصُّ: he exacts retaliation; applies qisas proportionately

ai.seo_question: How did Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام rule in a case where a killer survived an attempted qisas execution?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a case of qisas in which Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام corrected an initial ruling and clarified the proper legal procedure. It highlights precision in judicial retaliation, the authority of the Imam عليه السلام in judgment, and how recognition of the ruling led the claimant to pardon the offender.
